seoTitle: Air Conditioner BTU Calculator by Room Size
metaDescription: Estimate the cooling capacity in BTU/h for a room from floor area, ceiling height, sun exposure, occupants and kitchen use, with the 20 BTU per square foot rule.
intro: Choose a correctly sized air conditioner or heater by estimating the load of the room.
why:
The base is 20 BTU per square foot of floor area, scaled for ceilings above 8 feet, adjusted plus or minus 10% for very sunny or shaded rooms, plus 600 BTU for each occupant beyond two and 4,000 BTU for a kitchen. The result is shown in BTU/h, kilowatts and tons.

This is a rule of thumb. Insulation, window area and climate change the real load, and for a whole house you should ask for a Manual J calculation. Oversized units switch on and off too often and remove humidity poorly.

No data is sent anywhere: the work happens in your browser, so you can use it offline once the page has loaded.
howTo: Enter the room area and ceiling height.
Pick a unit near the recommended capacity.

faq.q: How many BTU for 300 sq ft?
faq.a: About 6,000 BTU/h with the base rule.

faq.q: What is a ton of cooling?
Can I use it for heating?
faq.a: The factor is for cooling; heating needs depend on climate and insulation.
No. Everything is processed in your browser, and the page makes no network requests with your input.
